topic.title: Life of an API Request: Client to Database and Back

hook: What actually happens when your app calls fetch('/api/users')? Follow the complete network and server lifecycle.

slides.headline: The Life of an HTTP API Request: Step-by-Step
slides.body: When a frontend triggers an API call, the request traverses network gateways, SSL termination, reverse proxies, server middleware, and database pools before returning JSON.
slides.visualSuggestion: Client App firing HTTP request packet into network highway

slides.headline: Stage 1: DNS, TLS Handshake & Edge Gateways
slides.body: The browser resolves the domain via DNS and establishes an encrypted TLS 1.3 connection. The packet hits a Global Edge CDN or Reverse Proxy (e.g. Cloudflare / Nginx) for DDoS scrubbing and SSL offloading.
slides.visualSuggestion: Client -> Cloudflare Edge CDN -> Nginx Reverse Proxy

slides.headline: Stage 2: Server Pipeline & Middleware Execution
slides.body: The request reaches the Fastify/Node backend. Middleware parses headers, validates CORS policies, authenticates the JWT session token, and sanitizes the request body using Zod schemas.
slides.visualSuggestion: CORS Check -> Auth Token Verification -> Zod Schema Validator

slides.headline: Stage 3: Database Connection Pool & Query Execution
slides.body: The controller borrows an idle connection from the PgBouncer pool, executes an indexed SQL query against PostgreSQL, transforms the database rows into DTOs, and releases the connection.
slides.visualSuggestion: Fastify Handler -> PgBouncer Connection Pool -> PostgreSQL Engine

slides.headline: Stage 4: Response Serialization & Gzip Compression
slides.body: The server serializes the DTO into JSON, compresses the payload using Brotli or Gzip, attaches security headers (HSTS, Content-Security-Policy), and streams the 200 OK response back.
slides.visualSuggestion: JSON Serialization -> Gzip Compression -> HTTP 200 OK Stream

slides.headline: Summary: Resilient Architecture Powers Speed
slides.body: Understanding every hop in the request pipeline allows you to optimize latency at the right layer—from edge caching to connection pooling. Build systems with intention.

caption: Follow the journey of an HTTP API request! From DNS resolution and edge proxies down to database connection pooling and serialized response streams.
cta: Which step in this pipeline do you spend the most time optimizing? Save this post and follow @elevateweb.
sources: High Performance Browser Networking - Ilya Grigorik
